status.en: 7 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 42% fewer than the week before, most of them in Juba, Rumbek and Morobo.
status.nb: 7 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 42 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Juba, Rumbek og Morobo.

summary.en: Rebel forces clashed with government troops near the Uganda border, killing one and wounding three. In Tonj East, community leaders were detained and peace talks were launched to stop deadly communal violence, while Sudanese gunmen killed three South Sudanese refugees and injured seven, and a chief was injured in a land dispute in Juba. A UN envoy urged South Sudanese leaders to choose consensus over confrontation, and a documentary on local peacemaking was screened. Joseph Lagu, a South Sudan independence figure, died at age 94. The UCDP recorded 2 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Rebelstyrker kolliderte med regjeringsstyrker nær grensen til Uganda, og drepte én og såret tre. I Tonj East ble samfunnsledere arrestert og fredssamtaler startet for å stoppe dødelig vold mellom folkegrupper, mens sudanske væpnede menn drepte tre sørsudanesiske flyktninger og såret sju, og en høvding ble såret i en jordkonflikt i Juba. En FN-utsending oppfordret sørsudanesiske ledere til å velge konsensus fremfor konfrontasjon, og en dokumentar om lokalt fredsarbeid ble vist. Joseph Lagu, en sentral skikkelse i sørsudanesiske uavhengighetskampen, døde i en alder av 94. UCDP registrerte to dødsfall i væpnet konflikt i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
